t: Francis II created the hereditary Austrian imperial title in 1804, two years before he dissolved the Holy Roman Empire.
Under Metternich, Vienna led the conservative European order after 1815 and dominated both Germany and Italy.
Defeats in 1859 and 1866 ended Austrian power in Italy and Germany and led to the Compromise with Hungary in 1867.
dyk: Gregor Mendel, an Augustinian friar, presented his pea-plant experiments on heredity in Brünn, Moravia, in 1865; they were largely ignored until they were rediscovered in 1900.
ev: Francis II proclaims himself hereditary Emperor of Austria
Francis dissolves the Holy Roman Empire
Archduke Charles defeats Napoleon at Aspern-Essling before defeat at Wagram
The Congress of Vienna redraws Europe under Metternich's guidance
Revolutions drive Metternich into exile; Franz Joseph succeeds Ferdinand I
Hungarian forces surrender at Világos after Russian intervention
Prussia defeats Austria at the Battle of Königgrätz
The Compromise with Hungary creates Austria-Hungary

f.founder: Francis I (Holy Roman Emperor Francis II)
